title: Extraction and Detection of Free-Gossypol in Cottonseed Samples
author: Aparecido Almeida Conceição
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.krncv5e

steps.title: Dry cottonseed sample
steps.instruction: Place the cottonseed sample in a drying oven set to 40 °C and dry for 24 hours until completely dry.

steps.title: Grind dried sample to powder
steps.instruction: Grind the dried sample to a fine powder using an ultra‑centrifugal mill with a 0.5 mm screen; a bench mill may be used if the material is already well homogenized.

steps.title: Weigh powdered sample
steps.instruction: Weigh exactly 1 g of the powdered sample and transfer it into a 15 mL plastic centrifuge tube equipped with a screw cap.

steps.title: Add ultrapure water
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of Milli‑Q ultrapure water to the tube containing the powder.

steps.title: Vortex mixture
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube vigorously for about 10 seconds to obtain a homogeneous suspension.

steps.title: First sonication on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tube in an ultrasonic bath filled with ice (ice must fill the sonicator) and sonicate for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add HPLC‑grade acetone
steps.instruction: Add 7 mL of HPLC‑grade acetone to the tube.

steps.title: Second sonication on ice
steps.instruction: Again sonicate the mixture for 5 minutes in an ice‑filled ultrasonic bath.

steps.title: Second vortex mixing
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube vigorously for another 10 seconds to ensure complete mixing.

steps.title: Centrifuge at 9000 rpm
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 9000 rpm for 5 minutes at 8 °C.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer 2 mL of the clear supernatant to a fresh 15 mL centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Evaporate solvent
steps.instruction: Evaporate the solvent in a speed‑vacuum concentrator at room temperature, ensuring the temperature does not exceed 35 °C, until all solvent is removed.

steps.title: Resuspend residue in 70% acetone
steps.instruction: Prepare 70 % acetone with ultrapure water, then add 200 µL to the dried residue and vortex until the pellet is completely dissolved.

steps.title: Transfer to Eppendorf tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the resulting solution to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Eppendorf tube at 14 000 rpm for 10 minutes at 8 °C.

steps.title: Transfer final supernatant
steps.instruction: Move the clear supernatant into an autosampler vial for UHPLC analysis.

steps.title: Install C18 UHPLC column
steps.instruction: Mount a reversed‑phase C18 column (100 × 2.1 mm, 2.6 µm particle size) in the UHPLC system equipped with a photodiode array detector.

steps.title: Set column temperature
steps.instruction: Set the column oven to 35 °C.

steps.title: Prepare mobile phases
steps.instruction: Prepare mobile phase A as methanol and mobile phase B as water containing 0.1 % (v/v) trifluoroacetic acid (TFA).

steps.title: Program gradient elution
steps.instruction: Program the gradient: start at 60 % A (40 % B) and increase linearly to 100 % A by 8 min; hold 100 % A until 10 min; at 10.01 min switch back to 60 % A and hold isocratically until 14 min.

steps.title: Set sample tray temperature
steps.instruction: Set the autosampler tray temperature to 8 °C.

steps.title: Configure PDA detection
steps.instruction: Set the photodiode array detector to monitor at 254 nm.

steps.title: Inject sample
steps.instruction: Inject 2 µL of the prepared sample; the free‑gossypol peak should appear at ~6.3 min when analyzed with Empower software.

steps.title: Set UHPLC flow rate
steps.instruction: Set the mobile phase flow rate to 0.4 mL/min.
